extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for Royal Society Open Science (prospective and invited referees)
extracted.subtask_short: reviewing for Royal Society Open Science
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing peer review for Royal Society Open Science: a soundness-focused, single-anonymized journal that publishes reviewer reports openly. Emphasizes assessment of technical correctness and constructive, non-hostile reviewer behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness-based review (not impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal publishes research on the basis of objective peer review and accepts all articles that are "scientifically sound and useful to the community without assessing novelty or potential impact."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows the PLOS ONE / Royal Society Open Science / Scientific Reports model that focuses purely on technical correctness rather than perceived importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on methodology and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the methodology and conclusions are rigorous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal's approach focuses on whether the methodology and conclusions are rigorous, with importance/novelty assessment left to readers post-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assess novelty or potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not assess novelty or potential impact when deciding whether to accept articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importance/novelty assessment is explicitly left to readers after publication; acceptance is based on scientific soundness and usefulness to the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-anonymized peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal operates single-anonymized peer review: reviewers know authors' identities but reviewer identities are withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are encouraged to waive their right to anonymity and sign their reports; reviewer identities are withheld unless reviewers choose to reveal them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct: objective and constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should be objective and constructive in their assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise content-based critique and constructive suggestions for improvement rather than value judgments about the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct: focus on content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should be focused on the content of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the manuscript's scientific soundness, methods, data, analysis, and conclusions rather than extraneous factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on hostile, defamatory or derogatory comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must refrain from being hostile or inflammatory and must not make libellous or derogatory personal comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should avoid personal attacks and defamatory language; criticisms should be professional, evidence-based, and targeted at the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review (public reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer reports are made public alongside published articles under open peer review via Web of Science Transparent Peer Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision letters and author responses are also accessible; referee reports are published under an open access licence (CC-BY). Reviewers should therefore be aware their reports may be public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reviewers required
rubrics_metrics.description: At least two peer reviewers will be sought for each manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may request additional reviewers to assess the manuscript if needed.
